target_customer: Patients with FSHD, fibrosis and cancers, reached through eventual drug approval or pharma partnering
problem: Transcription factors drive many diseases but were considered undruggable; Altay targets allosteric sites with oral small molecules.
business_model: Pre-revenue drug developer funded by venture, patient foundation and grant money

founders.name: Osman Ozes
prior_employers: Led the first drug development program for Esbriet (Pirfenidone), employer not named on the YC page
education: Ph.D. (title shown on company site; school not stated)

founders.name: Ali Ozes
education: Ph.D. (title shown on company site; school not stated)
founders.background_notes: Role listed as CEO by one database and CSO on the company site; the company site is used.

technical_complexity.rationale: Drugging transcription factors with allosteric small molecules is research grade and needs preclinical and clinical development.

defensibility.rationale: Patents on molecules and discovery know how, but unproven in clinic at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied the programs per sources found; Bristol Myers Squibb (2021) and Astellas (2023) gave Golden Ticket recognitions per the company site.

market_need_then: Founders cite liver fibrosis affecting over 20 million Americans and a market over 30 billion dollars (YC page). Esbriet is cited as proof that fibrosis drugs sell.

branding.domain_note: Uses altaytherapeutics.com; one source also lists altaytx.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline Innovating Therapeutics for Unmet Medical Need

branding.community_and_virality: Patient community ties through FSH Friends and SOLVE FSHD.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand-specific press; identified mostly by science and funders.

pivots.from: Chronic liver diseases such as liver fibrosis and liver cancer (YC page)
pivots.to: Lead program DUX4 inhibitor for FSHD plus STAT3 inhibitor
pivots.why: Not stated; SOLVE FSHD invested September 2022 for FSHD inhibitors per company site

outcome_analysis: Altay is active and still preclinical as of 2026. It lived on small seed money, grants and foundation funding for several years, then announced a 37 million dollar Series A in October 2026 to take its oral DUX4 inhibitor toward the clinic. The pivot from liver disease to FSHD followed patient foundation funding.
notes: Series A reported by RARE Daily, a SOLVE FSHD press release and AllSci; an SEC Form D (Oct 2026) listed 15.7M sold so far, conflicting with the 37M announced total. Seed amounts conflict (about 3M or about 7M from SOLVE FSHD), so no amount recorded. YC listing shows investors as support logos only. Competitor search surfaced only current MASH companies, none dated near 2020, so the list is empty. Pivot date approximate. Ph.D. titles come from the company team page without schools.
